transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

In meetings I keep jumping in over people and cutting them off before I can stop myself. It is starting to impact my professional relationships, and despite my best efforts to practice self-discipline, I just can't seem to control it.
Beyond these difficulties with impulsivity, have you felt persistently down, sad, or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a year?

No, I wouldn't say I feel persistently sad, depressed, or irritable at all. My struggles are really just centered around this constant restlessness, my impulsivity, and keeping my focus during meetings.
Besides the impulsivity you mentioned, do you also frequently struggle with staying organized, losing items, or having trouble sustaining focus on tasks that aren't particularly stimulating?

Yes, those are actually huge struggles for me. In long meetings, I can only stay focused for about 15 or 20 minutes before my mind drifts or I get distracted by something minor like a phone lighting up. My assistant even jokes that I'd lose my head because I'm constantly leaving folders behind, forgetting to sign documents, or missing scheduled appointments.
Looking back at your childhood, did you experience these same challenges with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity before the age of 12?

Yes, absolutely, these issues go all the way back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, my teachers were constantly moving my seat or sending notes home because I couldn't stay in my chair. I was always blurting out answers and talking over other kids, no matter how many times I was told to wait my turn.
